admission.justification: Weighed adopting MCP Apps/A2UI/WebMCP against retaining the sandboxed canvas/dashboard host, binding future UI protocol adoption to harness standardization and security parity triggers.

alternatives.option: Retain the sandboxed opaque-origin canvas review iframe (canvas/protocol.py) and FastAPI/Vite dashboard host (serving/app.py) without adopting MCP Apps, A2UI, or WebMCP in Wave 1.
alternatives.reason: Preserves the verified opaque-origin sandbox, connect-src 'none' CSP, offline kit manifest checks, and zero-credential/parent-frame boundary across all harnesses without tying review rendering to immature client UI protocols (D1006, D1078).

alternatives.option: Adopt MCP Apps, A2UI, or WebMCP as the interactive host protocol for review and dashboard surfaces (D1006).
alternatives.reason: Harness support for MCP Apps, A2UI, and WebMCP is fragmented and does not yet guarantee equivalent opaque-origin sandboxing, offline asset verification, and zero credential exposure.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Primary user harnesses standardize stable MCP Apps, A2UI, or WebMCP rendering with documented opaque-origin sandboxing, offline asset integrity verification, and zero dashboard credential or parent-frame exposure.

consequences: Review explainers continue to render inside the dashboard's sandboxed iframe over canvas/protocol.py.
MCP Apps, A2UI, and WebMCP adoption stays deferred to Wave 2 pending harness standardization and security parity.
context: Interactive review pages run in an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe served by the dashboard FastAPI host (serving/app.py) over a narrow frame message protocol (canvas/protocol.py) with a manifest-verified offline kit. D1006 and Council #6 (D1078) weighed retaining this sandboxed dashboard/canvas host against adopting emerging MCP Apps, A2UI, or WebMCP host protocols.
